VERDICT: LGTM

The change places the display-formatting logic in exactly the right unit. `OwnerTelephone` is already the designated single source of truth for the owner-telephone domain, and `toDisplay` is the natural inverse of the existing `toE164` — it reuses the same `NATIONAL_LENGTH` key set to identify the country calling code rather than hardcoding or duplicating codes, so the two operations can't drift apart on which codes are recognized. No duplication, and the class stays a focused telephone utility rather than a catch-all.

The `OwnerMapper` addition follows the established sibling pattern precisely: a `@Mapping(... qualifiedByName)` entry plus a thin `@Named` default delegating to the static helper, matching `identityKey`, `checkDigit`, `ageBand`, etc. The private `groupInThrees` helper is a reasonable extraction kept appropriately private. The OpenAPI entry mirrors the other derived `readOnly` fields.

Minor, non-blocking: the class-level Javadoc still frames `OwnerTelephone` solely around the E.164 conversion rule and names only `toE164`'s two callers; a future maintainer might appreciate a one-line mention that the class also formats back out for display. Not a structural problem.
